cause: after the question was approved and the first ideas filed

3-check-that-face-embedding-agreement-pr.line: Every other idea is judged by this number, so it must be shown to match the owner's eye first.

why.impact: If agreement does not predict 'same person', no comparison in the notebook means anything.
why.odds: Face cosine usually separates same from different people, but thresholds shift with model and style.
why.path: Ideas 4 to 15 all wait for it.

13-judge-krea-2-loras-on-krea-2-turbo-no.line: Settles which Krea 2 model every Krea measurement is made on before many are made.

why.impact: If Raw and Turbo rank settings differently, Krea results measured on Raw would mislead.
why.odds: Krea's card says Raw LoRAs are meant for Turbo, so a difference is plausible but unmeasured.
why.path: Sets the measuring model for every later Krea 2 comparison.

14-pick-the-checkpoint-automatically-by-.line: Every training comparison needs a fair rule for which checkpoint stands for a run.

why.impact: Without it, comparisons between setups depend on hand-picked steps, and the shipped recipe needs it anyway.
why.odds: Suite agreement should track the best step, though leakage penalties are untuned.
why.path: Second round (15) and every training-setting comparison lean on it.

4-which-model-draws-the-most-consistent-.line: The training pictures are the biggest lever on text-route consistency.

why.impact: A drawer that keeps one face across angles likely sets the ceiling for the LoRA.
why.odds: Models differ a lot in sheet consistency; one should clearly lead.
why.path: Its winner becomes the starting point for 6, 8 and 9.

5-which-model-draws-the-most-faithful-re.line: The same lever for the reference route, where likeness counts more.

why.impact: Decides the reference route's whole dataset source.
why.odds: Edit models vary in identity drift; at least one should hold the reference.
why.path: Its winner is the base for 7.

10-vary-the-outfit-across-the-dataset-in.line: A well-known failure with a cheap fix, likely to come out positive.

why.impact: Fixes outfit binding, which shows in every generation that asks for other clothes.
why.odds: Spurious attribute binding is well documented and the default sheets wear one outfit.
why.path: Independent of the others once the metric exists.

7-include-the-reference-image-itself-in-.line: A cheap test of whether the real face anchors reference-route likeness.

why.impact: Could raise likeness, which the reference route weighs most.
why.odds: One real picture may anchor the face or be memorised; either is plausible.
why.path: Best run on the drawer chosen in 5.

9-upscale-sheet-panels-to-1024-pixels-be.line: Panels train small today; upscaling may lift quality cheaply.

why.impact: Mainly affects the quality constraint rather than consistency.
why.odds: Sharper input usually helps, but upscaler artefacts can be learned too.

6-choose-the-text-route-identity-by-clus.line: Tests whether sheet-level clustering overrates shared rendering.

why.impact: Changes how the text-route identity is chosen, not the whole pipeline.
why.odds: The shared-render worry is real but its size is unknown.
why.path: Best run on the drawer chosen in 4.

12-turn-on-protect-the-description-while.line: May cut leakage into plain 'person' images at some cost in speed.

why.impact: Helps flexibility and leakage more than core consistency.
why.odds: Preservation methods often reduce leakage but can weaken likeness.

11-rank-16-versus-rank-32-for-krea-2-and.line: A tuning knob; likely a small difference either way.

why.impact: Rank rarely makes or breaks a character LoRA.
why.odds: 16 matching 32 is plausible, but MOSS's settings are borrowed and untested.

8-fill-missing-head-angles-with-an-edit-.line: Edit-model filling risks drifting the face, and angle checking does not exist yet.

why.impact: Better angle coverage could help the hard front-to-profile case.
why.odds: Edit models tend to pull faces toward their own idea of a person.
why.path: Needs the drawer from 4 and a way to check panel angles.

15-train-a-second-round-on-images-the-fi.line: The final refinement; only meaningful once the rest of the pipeline is set.

why.impact: Could tighten consistency, but costs a full extra training run.
why.odds: The paper found it helps, though self-training drifts details and scenes.
why.path: Needs the checkpoint rule (14) and a settled pipeline.
